Blair.fun: Round 3, when my Owl list came back as Eagle, Mouser, Sphinx and Tit with no Hawk. That one result exposed Alex's fake Hawk claim right away.
Blair.change: A blocked or hugged role should get a clear line in its dawn report saying so. Then a blank result can't be confused with "nothing happened."
Blair.regret: In round 1 I treated Finley's true but unverifiable Turkey claim as suspicious and threw 5 cards, including my 10, at Finley. Drew's Hawk result was just as unverifiable. I should have pressed Drew harder and thrown only low cards when I wasn't sure.

Casey.confusing: Finley's -1 in round 3. No role in this game takes eggs, so I didn't immediately see that a confused report could show a loss. It's also not obvious that a confused player actually discards cards based on a fake count.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when Drew copied my Tit claim word for word and said I was the copy. I could point out that I'd claimed first, and the table still came together on Alex, the cat everyone could prove.
Casey.change: I'd give Farm players a little more consolation for a wrong eggsecution, or make it more visible how much a lost round costs. Round 1 decided the whole game: Drew banked 47 on one fake claim nobody could check.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I started the push on Finley's unverifiable Turkey claim and threw my 13 and 9. I should have pointed out that nothing could check Drew's Hawk result either, and I should have thrown only low cards on such thin evidence.

Drew.confusing: Finley's -1 in round 3. No animal takes eggs, so I couldn't tell if it was a real change or only the confused report. The rules don't clearly say whether the nest-size list shows a confused player's fake change.
Drew.fun: Round 1. My Hawk claim fit Alex's Falcon info and Ellis's confusion so cleanly that the whole table, including Finley, threw at a Farm player. I banked 47 points from it.
Drew.change: Announcing every score between rounds showed I had won as Meowfia with a fake Hawk claim. After that the whole table visited me every night. Showing only rankings, or hiding which side earned the points, would stop one round from giving away a player's past alignment.
Drew.regret: In round 3, naming Kookaburra sent me to Finley, where everyone else also went. Blair's Owl listed a Sphinx there, which narrowed the cats down to me, Alex or Casey. I should have named a role nobody else would visit, like the Owl, so I'd stay off that list.

Ellis.confusing: The rules say a confused report is wrong, but my dawn report only said it "may be wrong." I wasn't sure whether I could rule Casey out as the Sphinx or should just ignore the info.
Ellis.fun: In round 2 five of us said one after another that we'd visited Drew and come back blank. It became obvious Drew was the Floofer hugging his visitors, and it felt great to watch that come together.
Ellis.change: Have the confusion message say plainly how it affects the info. For example, "the animal you learned is definitely wrong" or "your egg count is off by N."
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I trusted Drew because his visit matched my confusion. But being confused only proved that someone visited me, not that they were a Hawk. Finley.confusing: A confused report still makes you draw or discard for real. My fake -1 in round 3 showed up in the public nest sizes, so a wrong report became evidence the table could see, and Casey questioned me over it.
Finley.fun: Round 2: five of us said we visited Drew and came back blank, which made Drew the Floofer. That let me throw all six cards with confidence and jump from 4 to 60 points.
Finley.change: I'd give the Turkey something it can show when nobody visits it. An unverifiable "stayed home" claim made me the obvious target in round 1, even though I was Farm.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I named both Casey and Drew as suspects but threw at Casey. I should have focused on Drew's Hawk claim, which nobody could check, and thrown at Drew. Separately, I mistakenly sent my round 3 throw twice. Both calls were the same, but I was only supposed to send it once.

review.title: The Leader Gets Visited
review.headline: A fake Hawk banks 47 points, then five visits in a row expose the Floofer.
review.summary: In round 1 Drew was the only cat, the Mouser. He claimed Hawk on his real visit, and the table eggsecuted Finley, the Turkey, because nobody could check his stay-home claim. Drew banked 47. In round 2 everyone visited Drew because he was the leader. He was the Floofer, so all five came back hugged and blank, and he was caught at once. Finley had kept his high cards when he was voted out in round 1, threw all six at Drew and banked 60. By round 3 nests were tiny. Blair's Owl list disproved Alex's fake Hawk claim, and Finley held on to win 66 to 51.

rounds.recap: Drew (Mouser) visited Ellis and claimed Hawk. Alex's Falcon result and Ellis's real confusion both seemed to confirm that claim. Every visit claim fit together except Finley's Turkey stay-home, so the table voted Finley, who was Farm. Drew threw all five cards and banked 47.

All five Farm players visited Drew because he led with 47 and had been Meowfia last round. Drew was the Floofer, so every visitor was hugged and got no info. Five blank reports made the vote obvious after one beat, and Finley banked 60 from the high cards he kept in round 1.

As Sphinx, Drew saw only 4 Farm roles in play, worked out that there were 2 cats, and picked Kookaburra to confuse Finley. Alex (Mouser) claimed Hawk on Finley, but Blair's Owl list (Eagle, Mouser, Sphinx, Tit) had no Hawk. Drew counterclaimed Casey's Tit to muddy things, but the table put every vote on the provable lie, Alex.

highlights.text: Drew's fake Hawk claim matched his real visit, so Alex's Falcon result and Ellis's confusion both seemed to confirm it, and he banked 47.
Facing a vote he knew he would lose, Finley threw only his S8 and kept five high cards, which became his game-winning 60 next round.
Blair's Owl list of Eagle, Mouser, Sphinx and Tit sank Alex's Hawk claim within one beat.
Drew claimed Tit, word for word like Casey, to make it a coin flip between them. It nearly split the table, but everyone held on Alex.

confusions.what: Said Blair's +1 'can't be explained' and asked Blair to claim, right after Blair had claimed Eagle and explained the egg. This may come from players in the same group acting at once.
Gave 'no egg went into Drew's nest' as proof of the hug. An Owl only lays an egg when nobody else visited, and Blair had already claimed a visit to Drew, so no egg was expected anyway.
Thought Finley's -1 was impossible because no animal steals eggs. A confused report can force a real discard.
Called the -1 'just the fake report', but the discard really happened. Finley lost one of only two cards to confusion.

worked: Owl: listing the visiting animals by name, not by player, disproved a role claim in round 3 and gave Farm a fair, solvable puzzle.
Sphinx: learning the Farm roles in play let Drew deduce that there were 2 cats and pick a smart target (the Kookaburra). That was real reasoning from a cat ability.
Kookaburra confusion as cover: in round 1 Ellis's real confusion seemed to confirm the Mouser's fake Hawk claim, so a careful bluff could work.
The kept-card and consolation economy produced real throw decisions: Finley's 1-card throw while losing, Casey keeping a Wild, Drew keeping his 9.
problems: Score snowball plus targeting the leader: a lone cat who wins round 1 banks around 47, and everyone can tell they were Meowfia. Next round every player visits them on reflex. One round decided the leaderboard. Fix: cap points banked per round, or give the leader a disadvantage.

Floofer exposes itself: it hugs everyone who visits it, and the hugged players' reports come back blank. When several players visit, the Floofer is caught instantly, as in round 2. Fix: give hugged players a normal-looking report (for example a plausible fake), or hug only one visitor.

The Mouser's Wink was never used in two tries. CAW CAW ended days after beat 1 or 2, before Alex got a second turn in round 3. Fix: allow CAW only from beat 3, or let the Wink be used at night or at the vote.

Turkey is the default scapegoat: a Turkey with no visitors has a claim nothing can confirm, and it looks exactly like a cat's cover story. The table voted for it as 'the one claim nothing touches'. Fix: give the Turkey some info it can share, for example that it learns it had no visitors in a way others can check.

Nests shrink until the last round barely matters: nests only gain 2 cards per round. By round 3 players held 1-4 cards, so the final round could not change the leader. Confusion also cost Finley one of his two cards, which is harsh. Fix: deal more cards each round. Separately, clean up the log: it has debug lines like 'no effect at tier 50' and a blank target for Drew's round 3 visit.
